title: Torsors under torsion local systems are local systems
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] and work on its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Let $G$ be a sheaf of abelian groups which is a torsion local system, and let $T$ be a sheaf of sets with a free $G$-action such that the quotient sheaf $T/G$ is a local system. Then $T$ is a local system. Here local system [def-per-ind-finite-etale-local-system] means that the underlying sheaf of sets is a filtered colimit of sheaves represented by finite etale $X$-schemes [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], and torsion means that every germ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] at a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point] is killed by some positive integer (the bound may depend on the germ).

proof.text: Put $Y=T/G$ and write $Y=\bigcup_iY_i$ as a filtered union of finite local-system subsheaves, using the set-local-system theorem. Set $T_i=T\times_Y Y_i$. The restricted $G$-action is free and has quotient $Y_i$: a local section of $Y_i$ lifts locally along the quotient map, and two lifts differ locally by $G$. Every local section of $T$ lands locally in some $Y_i$, so $T=\varinjlim_iT_i$ as set sheaves. Thus closure under ambient colimits reduces the problem to finite $Y$. If $Y$ is empty, $T$ is empty and already finite etale.

source.place: XVII Lemma 7.2.6, p. 302, first paragraph; XVII 7.2.4 for ambient colimit closure.

proof.text: Represent finite $Y$ by a finite etale $q:Y\to X$. This $Y$ is Noetherian: a finite algebra is of finite type (a finite module generating list also generates it as an algebra), so the finite-type-over-Noetherian theorem applies. Under the slice equivalence of the set-local-system theorem, $T\to h_Y$ becomes a sheaf $\widetilde T$ on $Y_{\mathrm{et}}$ with free $q^{-1}G$-action and terminal quotient. It is therefore a $q^{-1}G$-torsor: the terminal quotient gives local sections, and freeness plus the quotient condition gives unique local differences, which glue by uniqueness. The same theorem says $q^{-1}G$ is a local system; it remains torsion since the inverse-image stalk theorem gives, for every geometric point $\bar y$ of $Y$, an isomorphism of abelian groups $(q^{-1}G)_{\bar y}\simeq G_{q\bar y}$. Once the torsor case is proved on the Noetherian scheme $Y$, $q_!\widetilde T\simeq T$ is a local system by its total-space clause. Hence it suffices to prove the torsor case over an arbitrary Noetherian base.

source.place: XVII Lemma 7.2.6, p. 302, reduction through q_!; finite type: Stacks Tag 01T6, lemma-finite-type-noetherian.

proof.text: Now $T$ is a $G$-torsor. Write $G=\varinjlim_iG_i$ using the finite-subsystem lemma. The Noetherian base is quasi-compact by definition and quasi-separated by the locally-Noetherian quasi-separatedness theorem. The cohomology-colimit theorem therefore applies in degree one, without a uniform exponent assumption: $H^1(X,G)=\varinjlim_iH^1(X,G_i)$. The torsor classification sends $T$ to a class $c$; choose a stage class $c_i$ representing it, and a $G_i$-torsor $T'$ representing $c_i$. Write $G'=G_i$. Coefficient functoriality sends $c_i$ to the class of $P=G\wedge^{G'}T'$, where the contracted-product theorem supplies this torsor. Since both $P$ and $T$ have class $c$, injectivity of the torsor-class bijection gives a $G$-equivariant isomorphism $T\simeq P$.

source.place: XVII Lemma 7.2.6, p. 303, H^1 paragraph; Stacks Tags 03Q5 (lemma-colimit) and 03AJ (lemma-torsors-h1).

proof.text: For every finite locally constant subgroup $H\subseteq G$ containing $G'$, form $P_H=H\wedge^{G'}T'$. This is an $H$-torsor by the contracted-product theorem. By the definition of torsor it is etale locally isomorphic to $H$ by translation through a local section. Refine that cover by one on which $H$ is constant with finite group value. Then $P_H$ is constant with the same finite underlying set on that refinement, hence finite locally constant. The finite locally constant representability theorem makes $P_H$ a sheaf represented by a finite etale $X$-scheme.

source.place: XVII Lemma 7.2.6, p. 303, finite group torsors; Stacks Tag 03RV, lemma-characterize-finite-locally-constant.

proof.text: The finite subgroups $H$ containing $G'$ are cofinal in the filtered family of all finite subgroup systems: a common upper bound for $G'$ and any given finite subgroup lies in this subfamily. Thus their set-sheaf union is $G$. The contracted-product quotient gives compatible maps $P_H\to P$. To verify their colimit property, fix any set sheaf $E$. By the contracted-product universal property, compatible maps $P_H\to E$ are compatible morphisms $T'\times H\to E$ invariant under $(t,h)\mapsto(g'+t,h-g')$. They glue uniquely to an invariant morphism $T'\times G\to E$: locally a section of $G$ belongs to some $H$, and two such choices agree locally in a common upper bound. The same universal property now gives a unique map $P\to E$. Hence $P=\varinjlim_H P_H$. Each $P_H$ is finite etale representable by the preceding step, so $T\simeq P$ is a local system by its definition. This proves the torsor case used in Step 2, then the finite-quotient case and finally the general case of Step 1.

source.place: XVII Lemma 7.2.6, p. 303, final filtered contracted-product paragraph; universal property: Stacks Tag 03AJ, lemma-torsors-h1.
